### CVE-2019-9791
- Assigner: mozilla | Published: 2019-04-26 | Updated: 2024-08-04 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: Type inference is incorrect for constructors entered through on-stack replacement with IonMonkey
- Exploit-DB 46613: Spidermonkey - IonMonkey Type Inference is Incorrect for Constructors Entered via OSR (dos/multiple, 2019-03-26, verified=1)

The type inference system allows the compilation of functions that can cause type confusions between arbitrary objects when compiled through the IonMonkey just-in-time (JIT) compiler and when the constructor function is entered through on-stack replacement (OSR). This allows for possible arbitrary reading and writing of objects during an exploitable crash. This vulnerability affects Thunderbird < 60.6, Firefox ESR < 60.6, and Firefox < 66.

Affected:
- Mozilla / Thunderbird: affected unspecified <60.6 (custom)
- Mozilla / Firefox ESR: affected unspecified <60.6 (custom)
- Mozilla / Firefox: affected unspecified <66 (custom)

### CVE-2019-9792
- Assigner: mozilla | Published: 2019-04-26 | Updated: 2024-08-04 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: IonMonkey leaks JS_OPTIMIZED_OUT magic value to script
- Exploit-DB 46939: Spidermonkey - IonMonkey Leaks JS_OPTIMIZED_OUT Magic Value to Script (dos/multiple, 2019-05-29, verified=1)

The IonMonkey just-in-time (JIT) compiler can leak an internal JS_OPTIMIZED_OUT magic value to the running script during a bailout. This magic value can then be used by JavaScript to achieve memory corruption, which results in a potentially exploitable crash. This vulnerability affects Thunderbird < 60.6, Firefox ESR < 60.6, and Firefox < 66.

Affected:
- Mozilla / Thunderbird: affected unspecified <60.6 (custom)
- Mozilla / Firefox ESR: affected unspecified <60.6 (custom)
- Mozilla / Firefox: affected unspecified <66 (custom)

### CVE-2019-9816
- Assigner: mozilla | Published: 2019-07-23 | Updated: 2024-08-04 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: Type confusion with object groups and UnboxedObjects
- Exploit-DB 46940: Spidermonkey - IonMonkey Unexpected ObjectGroup in ObjectGroupDispatch Operation (dos/multiple, 2019-05-29, verified=1)

A possible vulnerability exists where type confusion can occur when manipulating JavaScript objects in object groups, allowing for the bypassing of security checks within these groups. *Note: this vulnerability has only been demonstrated with UnboxedObjects, which are disabled by default on all supported releases.*. This vulnerability affects Thunderbird < 60.7, Firefox < 67, and Firefox ESR < 60.7.

Affected:
- Mozilla / Thunderbird: affected unspecified <60.7 (custom)
- Mozilla / Firefox: affected unspecified <67 (custom)
- Mozilla / Firefox ESR: affected unspecified <60.7 (custom)

### CVE-2019-11708
- Assigner: mozilla | Published: 2019-07-23 | Updated: 2025-10-21 | Max CVSS: 10
- CWE: sandbox escape using Prompt:Open; CWE-20 CWE-20 Improper Input Validation
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 10 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=active, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- **CISA KEV**: added 2022-05-23, ransomware=Unknown — Mozilla Firefox and Thunderbird Sandbox Escape Vulnerability
- Exploit-DB 47752: Mozilla FireFox (Windows 10 x64) - Full Chain Client Side Attack (local/windows_x86-64, 2019-12-07, verified=0)

Insufficient vetting of parameters passed with the Prompt:Open IPC message between child and parent processes can result in the non-sandboxed parent process opening web content chosen by a compromised child process. When combined with additional vulnerabilities this could result in executing arbitrary code on the user's computer. This vulnerability affects Firefox ESR < 60.7.2, Firefox < 67.0.4, and Thunderbird < 60.7.2.

Affected:
- Mozilla / Firefox ESR: affected unspecified <60.7.2 (custom)
- Mozilla / Firefox: affected unspecified <67.0.4 (custom)
- Mozilla / Thunderbird: affected unspecified <60.7.2 (custom)
